answer: A voyage across an agent economy should cost more than a fake passport. Require every agent to lock a marble-sized bond of real value before it can trade, and tie that bond to one long-lived identity. A Sybil attacker must fund a fresh bond for every fake agent, so each copy costs real money, while an honest agent keeps its one bond working through the tundra of slow, cold markets. Copies that behave badly lose their bond, so mass fakery becomes ruinously expensive while honest participation stays cheap.
